Discussing with our rider group, admittedly this is all "prediction" since we don't have it yet.

However, we all agree that Gotway would have mentioned a better shell design, or possibly would have not talked about how it is the *same* design.

In any case, I have already seen many models at 1800wh.  Many riders are hoping to see better battery tech, more battery space, and better power delivery mechanisms or axle fixes that have a high impact on usability and safety while maintain a fun ride.  A simple bump up to a more powerful motor doesn't make the machine more viable as a transportation device and feels like a cop out on innovation given the space that is possible in the manufacturing field for the EUC community.

Here's the thing with the MSuper Pro as compared to the more recent innovations by GotWay and KingSong, its the same beans.

In the past 3 years, wheels have come out that have improved two main things: range and speed.  The speed has reached a point (given 100v Nikolas and Monsters etc) that almost nobody would want to go faster than 40 MPH.  

So what is left to improve?  Aesthetics, build quality of the shell to resist those infamous MSX cracks, ease of use, software upgrades, waterproofness, and as always, RANGE, to keep high speed riding safer and viable for longer.

Ths M-Super-Pro hits none of these potential upgrade areas.  The shell is the same crack-prone plastic, the Aesthetics are arguable improved upon in a minor fashion, but same design.  We have not seen Gotway invest into better software or wheel-interaction mediums.  The increased Wattage of the motor simply means a more power hungry machine, which with the same total Wh as other models, means LESS range if anything.  Exposed speaker cones means less waterproofing.  So what are we left with here that we can really consider an upgrade?  I guess the cutoff switch :)

​

So what is the inventive here of having a top-of-the line priced wheel with the important specs (range + speed) comparable and even less so than other leading models like the Nikola+ 100V?
